pr_title: terraform: Compare locks and provider requirements
pr_body: When building a context, we read the dependency locks and ensure that the provider requirements from the configuration can be satisfied. If the configured requirements change such that the locks need to be updated, we explain this and recommend running "terraform init". This check is ignored for any providers which are locally marked as in development. This includes unmanaged providers and those listed in the provider installation `dev_overrides` block. Fixes #26565. ### Screenshot
pr_comments:
There's a failing e2e test:

```
=== FAIL: command TestPlan_init_required (0.00s)
    plan_test.go:879: wrong error message in output: 
        Error: Provider requirements cannot be satisfied by locked dependencies
        
        The following required providers are not installed:
        
        - registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/test ()
        
        Please run "terraform init".
```

I'm not sure if this is a test that needs to be updated or if we need to somehow cope with this use case.
The above comment was a misread of test output. I'll investigate these test failures and re-request review if I can address them.

issue_context.title: Pinned required_providers version ignored by terraform plan
issue_context.body:
When changing the pinned version of a required provider, `terraform plan` happily ignores it.

### Terraform Version

```
Terraform v0.13.4
```

### Expected Behavior

`terraform plan` fails and tells me to run `terraform init` to update the provider.

### Actual Behavior

A plan is happily produced from invalid code.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a directory and put a similar config in a `main.tf` file:
```terraform
terraform {
  required_version = "0.13.4"
  required_providers {
    github = {
      source  = "hashicorp/github"
      version = "3.0.0"
    }
  }
}

provider "github" {
  token        = var.github_token
  organization = "hashicorp"
}

resource "github_branch_protection" "terraform-master" {
  repository = "terraform"
  branch     = "master"
}

variable "github_token" {
  type = string
}
```
2. run `terraform init`
3. run `terraform plan -var "github_token=$GITHUB_TOKEN"`
4. see a nice plan
5. update the configuration file to bump the github provider version to `3.1.0`
6. run `terraform plan -var "github_token=$GITHUB_TOKEN"`
7. see a nice plan
8. run `terraform init`
10. run `terraform plan -var "github_token=$GITHUB_TOKEN"`
11. see 4 errors being reported instead of a nice plan
comments: Same issue here after upgrade github provider to version `3.1.0`

Thanks for reporting this, @odormond.

It sounds like Terraform 0.13 is missing the behavior from prior versions of making sure that the items cached in the `.terraform` directory match what was installed by the most recent `terraform init` and that in turn matches the current configuration.

For provider dependencies in particular 0.13 was a bit of a stepping-stone release because we knew that 0.14 was going to include an explicit lock file to allow Terraform to remember version selections in your version control system, so the same versions can be selected even across multiple working directories. It seems like we missed having an interim check to make sure things are consistent even though the lock file isn't present yet.

I expect the behavior will be different on the main branch now as we prepare for the first beta of 0.14. This'll be a good thing for us to test in 0.14.0-beta1 to see if the behavior is better and to fix up anything that's still not quite right about the locking behavior for commands other than `terraform init`.

Hi @apparentlymart!

Thanks for the feedback. It's much appreciated. I'll keep an eye on the 0.14 progress then.
